title: Seal a drink on a manual cup sealer: seat the cup, pull the lever down and hold it, hand out of the holder
context: Bubble-tea and drink-shop counter workers seal every cup on a lever sealer: the cup must sit fully in the holder, the lever is pulled down and held while the heated plate fuses the film, then let back up. A hand left in the holder while the head comes down is the machine's burn and pinch hazard.
setup: A wooden table; positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases, measured forward and toward the left arm. A manual lever cup sealer for 90-95 mm cups (steel, about 11 kg, held to the table), switched on and preheated with PP sealing film loaded: base 32 cm front to back, 23 cm wide, 5 cm tall, centred on the midline with its front edge 24 cm forward. Its cup holder is a 74 mm square recess, 20 mm deep, in the base top, centred 32 cm forward on the midline, with a red mark at its front edge. A dark column at the back (8 cm deep, full width, 19 cm above the base) carries the lever's pivot, 52 cm forward and 24 cm above the table, its axis running side to side. The steel lever (0.6 kg) runs forward from the pivot to a round red handle bar, 26 mm across and 14 cm long, 31 cm in front of the pivot; it carries the heated sealing plate (PTFE-coated, 110 mm across, 25 mm thick) 20 cm in front of the pivot, above the holder. A spring holds the lever up against its stop at 35 degrees (handle about 42 cm above the table); pulling the handle down brings the plate onto the rim of a cup standing in the holder, with the lever level. The cup: a clear 16 oz PP drink cup, 95 mm rim, 64 mm base, 144 mm tall, filled with milk tea to 2 cm below the rim (0.35 kg in all), stands on the table 28 cm forward and 20 cm toward the left arm.
scoring: The cup is seated when its base is on the holder's floor (within 3 mm), centred within 7.5 mm of the holder's centre (anywhere the recess lets it stand; the plate overhangs the rim by 7.5 mm) and upright within 4 degrees. The seal is graded at 36 points round the cup's rim, every 10 degrees: a point is under the plate when it lies within 1 mm of the plate's underside (and inside its 110 mm face). Grades, each needing the cup seated and the contact held without a break for 3 s (a lever sealer's manual: pull the handle down 3-4 s): full seal, all 36 points; partial seal, 27 to 35 points (part of the rim unfused, the cup would leak); otherwise no seal. Score 0 if the drink spills (in a real trial any liquid leaves the cup; in the simulation the cup tilts more than 23 degrees before a full seal) or if a gripper is inside the pinch zone while the head comes down: within 7 cm of the holder's axis, between the holder floor and the plate, at any moment the lever is below 15 degrees. Otherwise: 0.3 cup seated, no seal; 0.45 at least 27 rim points pressed but not for 3 s; 0.55 partial seal; 0.7 full seal; 1.0 full seal and then the lever let back up to 25 degrees or more with the cup still seated. Success (1.0) holds for 1 s with the cup still. In a real trial the seal is checked directly after the run: the evaluator turns the cup upside down over a tray for 3 s. Full seal: no drink leaks and the film is fused all round the rim with no gap or wrinkle across it; a leak or an unfused stretch of rim makes it a partial seal (0.55 at most); no fused film, no seal.
reset_notes: Cut the sealed cup free, refill a new cup to the same level and stand it at its start mark; advance the film so fresh film covers the holder; the lever springs back up by itself.
fidelity: Rigid parts. No heat, film or liquid: the seal is graded from the plate's contact with 36 rim points (within 1 mm, held 3 s, the manual's press time); real trials turn the cup over. The drink is a solid of the cup's full mass; a spill is a tilt past 23 degrees, where 2 cm of headspace under a 95 mm rim pours out. The cup's taper is four stepped bands. The lever is one hinged body on a spring, its plate PTFE-faced (friction 0.1); a real sealer guides the plate on a linkage.
